subject.title: Feature/Fix: Integrate lineage discovery and shadow accounting

question: Should this intermediate shadow integration land after exact-head proof despite its additional changed-corpus scan cost, or should it wait and land together with the later safety and performance slices?
rationale: The implementation deliberately trades temporary refresh latency for migration evidence; whether that operational cost is acceptable between stacked merges requires repository-owner intent rather than a correctness inference.

options.title: Prove and sequence the full stack
options.body: Require exact-head runtime evidence, merge the prerequisite first, and land this slice only with the safety and performance follow-ups ready to follow immediately.

options.title: Accept the temporary scan cost
options.body: Merge after the prerequisite while explicitly accepting potentially long changed-corpus refreshes because legacy totals remain authoritative.

options.title: Pause the integration slice
options.body: Keep this PR open until the shadow path can be reviewed as one bounded landing with the later controls and optimizations.

recommendation.title: Prove and sequence the full stack
recommendation.body: Require exact-head runtime evidence, merge the prerequisite first, and land this slice only with the safety and performance follow-ups ready to follow immediately.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner, steipete is the clearest available owner for the scanner architecture and acceptable availability tradeoff.
